chunks: Harun ibn Muslim from Mas'adah ibn Sadah from Ja'far from his father from his forefathers, peace be upon them, that Ali (peace be upon him) was asked about the fly that enters in
the throat of the fasting person, he said: 'There is no making up (fast) for him, for it is not food.'
ai.seo_question: Does a fly entering the throat break the fast of a Muslim?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes that the accidental ingestion of a fly does not break the fast, classifying it as a minor impurity rather than substantial food (*ta'am*). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of distinguishing between negligible natural occurrences and deliberate consumption, ensuring that fasting remains accessible and not burdened by trivialities. The chain of narration through the Imams underscores the continuity of this practical legal insight within the Ahl al-Bayt's tradition.
